summary: Qwen3.5 constructed the 96-wide TP-local in_proj_ba as GPTQ-Marlin even though Marlin repacking requires output width divisible by 64 and the reported checkpoint stores the two source weights as bf16. The model now disables GPTQ-Marlin only when this projection's TP-local output width violates that boundary, allowing the existing stacked bf16 loaders to consume in_proj_b.weight and in_proj_a.weight. Compatible widths and other quantizers remain unchanged.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before regression: the baseline passed GPTQ-Marlin through for incompatible TP-local widths 96 and 48; 2 tests failed and 3 boundary controls passed. Raw log: reports/j-fc63755e706a/raw/regression-before.log

16 focused tests passed: incompatible and compatible Marlin widths, TP-local boundary behavior, unchanged FP8/unquantized behavior, stacked bf16 weight loading, and existing quantization skip behavior. Raw log: reports/j-fc63755e706a/raw/focused-tests.log

Raw log: reports/j-fc63755e706a/raw/gpu-numerical.log

gpu_execution_evidence: reports/j-fc63755e706a/raw/gpu-numerical.log identifies AMD Instinct MI355X and gfx950:sramecc+:xnack- and records the independent numerical comparison.
remaining_limitations: The complete 27B checkpoint weights were not downloaded and the full HTTP server was not launched; checkpoint config and safetensors index metadata were inspected directly instead.

The assigned GPU is AMD gfx950, while the reported production crash used NVIDIA Marlin. The exact NVIDIA gptq_marlin_repack failure was therefore not executed locally; its enforced 64-column boundary and the faulty 96-column construction were exercised deterministically.
The GPU fixture validates this projection's bf16 loading and numerical execution only, not full-model semantic accuracy or distributed execution.
No native source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
The prepared interpreter does not include the ruff module; formatting was checked with git diff --check and the focused Python tests.
